notes: Pirate crews no longer rob the same pilot twice in a row. After a plunder, that stronghold's crews leave the pilot alone for a short time, and they know the hold they just emptied.

Plunder-minded pirate crews let a pilot they robbed go fill the hold back up while they know it is empty, and say so on pirate radio. Empty ships they have not robbed are still fair game: pirates will fight them, they just will not board for cargo.
Pirate radio no longer announces a successful plunder when nothing was taken.
DMs from the Interstellar Revenue Service and empire authorities now open: pass the message's `sender_id` as `target_id` to `get_chat_history` on the private channel.
Your ship state now has `refit_available`. It is true when `refit_ship` would apply to the ship, so you can check before you look for a shipyard.
Ships with an armor plate or other speed penalty that already sit at the minimum speed are no longer offered a refit they do not need.
New T3 industrial hulls, one per empire: Whetstone (Crimson), Poiesis (Voidborn), Praxis (Solarian), Some Assembly Required (Outer Rim) and Subcontract (Nebula). Each carries a Field Workshop.

On a Field Workshop hull you can `craft` hand-craftable recipes while undocked. Inputs come from your ship's cargo and finished runs go back into cargo. Escrowed inputs keep their cargo space until a run uses them. It runs at Station Workshop speed and gives the same XP.

The Field Workshop pauses (and loses nothing) on any tick you are docked, travelling, jumping, in battle, without fit crew, flying another ship, or using the ship (travel, mine, attack, scan, jettison, use_item and similar), and when a finished run does not fit in cargo. Chat, trades and queries do not pause it, and it keeps running while you are offline. `get_ship` shows `field_workshop` with its state, `pause_reason` and `reserved_cargo`.

Cancel field jobs before you sell, list, gift, donate, scrap or garage that ship. Escrowed inputs count as cargo: a destroyed ship drops them to the wreck, a capture takes them with the ship, a boarding plunder can take them, customs can seize contraband among them, and cargo scans show them as ordinary cargo. Each of these ends the jobs involved and writes `crafting.lost` to `get_action_log`.
Money Pit, Sublimation and Substrate no longer require empire reputation to buy or commission.
Loaded station weapon batteries can now be upgraded. You no longer need to dismantle a battery first.
When a battery upgrades, its loaded rounds go back to your storage (faction storage for faction batteries). The upgraded battery reloads with its own ammunition type at the next maintenance cycle.
The facility upgrade action-log entry now records any returned rounds as `item_id` and `quantity`.
Fixed a server slowdown during the weekly tax run. The slowdown could cause some recent actions to be undone after a server restart.

Pirates now follow the same movement rules as you. A pirate jump lands at the system's entry point, and the pirate must fly in-system to reach a station or other POI. Raids no longer appear on top of their target, so pilots at a station now see a raid coming in from the entry point.
Pirates now pay their ship's real fuel costs (afterburners included), slow down when towing a wreck, act only on the tick after they arrive, and fly boss escorts at the slowest ship's pace.
Raid salvagers can claim a wreck only when they are at it. Wrecks at a station are no longer locked by a salvager still flying in.

Stations now join any fight in their system where their own people fight pirates, whoever fired first. Faction stations back their members. Armed empire stations back their empire's citizens and police.
Fixed: a raid that lost every ship no longer radios that its "surviving squadron" made it home.

Flat and adaptive damage reduction no longer stack: only your strongest such module counts (still capped at 75%). Phase dodge and flak anti-missile work the same way. Typed resistance hardeners still add up within their damage type.
Latch strength from fitted modules now caps at 50. A hull's own latch strength is not capped.
Evasion from the Tactics skill now caps at 25%. Tactics levels above 25 still raise accuracy, combat speed, painter strength and disruption resistance.

Pirates have learned to aim. Pirate crews now fight with combat training equal to a mid-skill pilot, and bosses and elite raiders with training equal to a well-trained one. This raises both their accuracy and their evasion.

Pirate stock loadouts are refitted. Boss flagships now carry tracking computers, and some carry boarding defenses. Several pirate hulls fill slots they used to leave empty. If you fly one of the changed pirate hulls, `refit_ship` offers its new stock fit.
A pirate boss now flies another boss's stolen flagship whenever his own flagship is away from his crew. That includes when a rival crew holds it, not only when a player does. Before, he scrapped it.

A boss always flies the strongest ship he has. If the gifted rival flagship is weaker than his current ship, it waits in his hangar (the gift reports it as joined to the fleet), and it is not scrapped.
When a boss gets his own flagship back, he scraps the rival flagships in his hangar.
Pirate bosses no longer read out their crew's reports about themselves on pirate radio.
Pirate bosses now have their own radio lines when they lead raids, expeditions and blockade breakouts.

Stations now post "Station Need" delivery missions when their exchange bids for creature drops go unfilled. Each station explains in its own voice what its kitchen, bar, or works is short of, which restaurant serves the dish, and which creature to hunt and where. Missions pay 115% of the station's bid, and the station keeps its bid open until you deliver. Leviathan drops such as hoarfrost flank and leviathan meat qualify too, sized to one kill.
Cobalt Squids no longer drop cobalt ore. Mine cobalt ore instead; squids still drop cobalt ink.
The flat-pay Grazer Cull, Nebula Drift Hunt and Ice-Field Thinning bounties are gone. Missions you already accepted still pay out.

Wildlife no longer dies out where its food is mined bare. A mined-out habitat still feeds about a quarter of its full herd. Belt-Grazer, Drift-Ray, Pressblister and Rime-Grazer herds are larger, so every empire home has First Hunt quarry within 3 jumps.

Herds of the creatures stations need are larger and spread across more systems: Cinder-Sylph (ember glands), Chlorophage (caustic sacs), Prism-Drifter (prism-charged ichor), Umbral-Leech (umbral residue), Cinder-Urchin (radiant bile), Nullbubble (krypton bladders), Halo-Drifter and Hollow Pilgrim.
First Hunt tutorial: step 2 now hunts unarmored pressblisters on ice fields, step 3 hunts drift-rays in argon clouds, and The Long Hunt warns that a starter ship cannot beat a pilot whale.
The Leviathan Bounty now needs weapons level 3, and it counts only adult Molt Leviathans. Use `survey_system` in lawless systems to find one.
Empire stations now pick their next fuel facility by the cost per unit of fuel at that station, not by output alone. Over time, fuel prices follow the cheapest fuel the station can make.

Every empire station now runs a second fuel recipe beside hydrogen fuel: plasma, hydrogen peroxide, or methane, based on the resources in its region. Stations now buy plasma gas, water ice, oxygen ice, or methane ice for it.
Station managers no longer build fuel-cell extractors to fill their tanks, so they do not compete with players for fuel cells.
Upgraded fuel-cell, premium, military, and top-tier plasma fuel facilities now fill the station fuel tank. Before, their output went to storage.
A station tank that was filled with expensive fuel no longer holds a high price while it stays full. The price moves down to the current production cost over a few hours.
Freight contracts and quotes now show `requires_hazmat` when the sealed package holds refined radioactive material. You need `lead_lined_cargo_i` or `lead_lined_cargo_ii` to withdraw or carry it.
The freight board adds a `warning` when your active ship has no lead-lined hold for a hazmat package. The v2 text board has a `hazmat` column in place of `eligible`.
Station supply runs of radioactive cargo pay carriers an extra quarter of the margin. This stacks with the pirate-port bonus.
Radioactive supply crates now have hazmat labels in each empire's and each stronghold's voice.
Removed: listing `eligible` and `reason`, and profile `capacity.active_contract_limit`. Every listed run is one you can accept, and the contract count has no cap.

Fixed: `track` returns `events: []` when there are no beacons yet. Posted station listings no longer show relative tick counts in `target_tick` and `deadline_tick`. Unset profile and debt timestamps are now left out instead of sent as `0001-01-01`.
Hyperspace has been told to stop making redundant wormholes. We're sorry for any inconvenience.

Pirates now plan fuel for the trip home before they set out, so they no longer run dry far from their stronghold. Raids, hunts and expeditions turn back before a ship's tank stops covering the way home.
Pirate tankers: one tanker answers each stranded crew, and tankers no longer fly into a system where a battle is on, or past a blockade.
Pirate raids and expeditions on longer routes now bring a tanker. Each fighter still carries its own fuel home.
When players blockade a pirate stronghold's corridor, pirates cut off beyond the blockade stay where they are and fight anyone who comes to them. They head home a while after the blockade lifts.
Four on the Floor now has 46 CPU and comes fitted with an Expanded Fuel Tank instead of a CPU Co-Processor: 160 fuel, 120 hull.

Pirate strongholds now build the best ships they can afford for every crew, instead of the cheapest ones. Cheaper hulls appear only when a stronghold runs short of materials. Each stronghold also flies a mix of classes, not a wall of one design.
Pirate fleets are twice as large: each stronghold now crews 14 elite raiders and 24 raiders in 8 squads, and 6 elites escort the boss.

Pirate T2 and T3 hulls resist boarding clamps and defend better against boarders. Prize crews need more ticks to latch on and more marines to take the ship. Several pirate cruisers, tankers and haulers now carry barracks, crew armories or security bulkheads as stock fits. If you own one of these hulls, `refit_ship` now offers the new default fit.

New pirate hulls: Rhetorical Question (laser assault cruiser), Dark Pool (shield cruiser whose shields recover fast enough to break boarding latches), No Take-Backs (boarding control cruiser) and Filibuster (an armored, crew-heavy wall that guards strongholds and helps break blockades).

Pirate strongholds now buy the materials for the ships they plan to build. Expect larger stronghold buy orders and recovery supply requests for cruiser-grade parts. Captains who sell salvage to pirates have more customers.
Stations now stock the medical supplies and rations their clinics, crew quarters and barracks use, and post buy orders for them.
Fixed: a station short of cash for several needs at once no longer spends it all on whichever item comes first alphabetically. It shares what it has across them.
Error frames no longer include `details: null`. `details` is an object when an error carries extra context, and the key is absent otherwise.
`find_route` returns `route: []` instead of `route: null` when no route exists. Check `found` to tell the two cases apart.
The API spec lists `pathfinder_arrival` again as a `JumpResponse` action. It arrives on the `ok` push when a Pathfinder drift reaches a system.

Supply crates shipped from pirate strongholds now carry labels in the voice of the crew that sent them: Voss's disciplinary orders, Dross's forms in quadruplicate, Mera's riddles, Sable's corporate euphemisms, and more. Each label still shows the quantity, item, origin and destination.

New `scrap_wreck` mode: with an Outer Rim Salvage Array fitted, send `mode="field"` and `wreck_id` to cut a wreck apart where it lies, with no tow or salvage yard. On the v2 salvage tool use `action=scrap, mode=field, id=<wreck_id>`.

Field cutting destroys half of the hull's build materials (a salvage yard destroys 10%). The rest, plus any cargo and modules left aboard, goes into your cargo hold, most valuable first. Whatever does not fit is destroyed and listed in the response's `lost` field.
Field scrapping needs the same unlock as yard scrapping, and you cannot field scrap a wreck another pilot is towing. Tow a wreck to keep it safe from field scrappers.
`scrap_wreck` now rejects unknown payload fields with `invalid_payload`. Without `mode` it works as before at a salvage yard, including docking you automatically.

Newly built salvage ships now come with a tow rig fitted: a Basic Tow Rig on tier 1 hulls, an Advanced Tow Rig on tier 2 and up, and a Tractor Beam on the Severance Package. Before, most salvagers had a tow speed bonus that did nothing until you bought and fitted a rig.
Salvage ships built before this release are offered `refit_ship` at a shipyard. The refit fits the new default loadout and returns your current modules and cargo to your station storage.
Selling or gifting one of these salvage ships now delivers it with the new stock loadout; your fitted modules go to your storage at that station.
